paras: The shooting of Alfred Williams was an attack on a Black pastor near Edgewood, Georgia, who was found in the woods on the morning of October 11, 1888, with over a hundred buckshot wounds that an Atlanta dispatch attributed to members of his own congregation. The dispatch said he was expected to die, and several papers headlined the story as a lynching or murder, but no report of his death was found.

Williams, styled "Dr." and described as "colored," was pastor of the Antioch colored church in Edgewood. Some time before the attack he had organized a cooperative store among his parishioners and served as its storekeeper. "Dissensions soon arose," and the store was placed in the hands of two receivers.

On the morning of Thursday, October 11, Williams was found in the woods with "over a hundred buckshot wounds in his body." According to the Atlanta dispatch, the wounds were "made by members of his congregation," who were not named or numbered. The dispatch ended with the prediction "He will die."
The coverage contains no later report of Williams's death or recovery, and no report of arrests, an inquest or a trial was found.

The story reached the press as a single Atlanta wire dispatch, which the San Antonio Daily Light printed on October 12 under "Murdered by His Flock." On October 13 The Sun in New York, the Waterbury Evening Democrat and the Wilmington Evening Journal ran it as "A Negro Pastor Lynched by His Flock," while the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer, the Annapolis Evening Capital and the Wichita Eagle headed it as a murder: "Murdered by His Congregation," "Murdered by His Parishioners" and "A Minister Murdered." These headlines declared a death that the dispatch beneath them did not report.

Over the following week a condensed version, "Preacher Riddled With Buckshot," appeared in Kentucky and Ohio weeklies and added that the congregation members were "hostile towards him." Shorter paragraphs ran in news digests in the Emporia Weekly News and two Vermont papers, one of which misplaced the town as "Edgeworth, N.C." None of the papers added comment, and no Georgia paper's account was found.

reader.title: Shooting of Alfred Williams
bases: A Black pastor was found shot with buckshot by members of his own congregation after a dispute over a cooperative store; no death is reported, though the wire said he would die (A1, A2, A3).

The wire says only that Williams 'will die' and no report of his death was found, the attackers are unnumbered 'members of his congregation', and the only motive suggested is a dispute over a store, not a claim of punishing a crime (A1, A2, A3).
Every report is a copy or condensation of one Atlanta wire dispatch; no local Georgia account or follow-up was found (A1, A2, A3).

accounts.label: Atlanta wire report
accounts.gist: After dissensions over his cooperative store, which went to two receivers, Williams was found in the woods with over a hundred buckshot wounds inflicted by members of his congregation; he was expected to die.

framing.detail: Papers ran the Atlanta wire unchanged under headlines ranging from 'A Negro Pastor Lynched by His Flock' (The Sun, Waterbury, Wilmington) to 'Murdered by His Flock' and 'Preacher Riddled With Buckshot', with no editorial comment.

versions.value: Found 'yesterday morning' in a dispatch dated Oct. 12 (i.e., Oct. 11)
Found 'Thursday morning' in a dispatch dated Oct. 13 (also Oct. 11)

conflicts.note: Both versions point to Thursday, Oct. 11; the two datelines are the same text. A digest reprint in the Middlebury Register (A10) said 'Friday', apparently a rewording error.

versions.value: Text: 'He will die' (still alive when the wire was sent)

conflicts.note: The headlines anticipate a death the dispatch does not report; no later report of his death was found.
